title: "interactive_map_complete"
format: html

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(plotly)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r}

#Reading Data
full_data_with_state <- readRDS("../data/full_data_for_interactive_map.rds")

#All unique months (chronologically)
unique_months <- sort(unique(full_data_with_state$month))

# Fixed color scale for each variable, so shades are comparable across months
gas_limits   <- range(full_data_with_state$MRA_Regular, na.rm = TRUE)
unemp_limits <- range(full_data_with_state$unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE)

# Empty list which is then filled with both maps
plotly_plots <- list()

# For loop to create a different pair of maps for each month
for (i in seq_along(unique_months)) {
  # Filtering for the unique month
  month_variable <- unique_months[i]
  full_data_with_state_specific_month <- full_data_with_state |>
    filter(month == month_variable)

  # Left map: Gas Prices (blue)
  Gasplot <- ggplot(full_data_with_state_specific_month,
                    aes(geometry = geom, fill = MRA_Regular,
                        text = paste0(
                          "State: ", State,
                          "<br>Gas Price: $", round(MRA_Regular, 3)))) +
    geom_sf() +
    scale_fill_distiller(type = "seq", direction = 1, limits = gas_limits) +
    theme_void() +
    labs(fill = "Gas ($/gal)")

  # Right map: Unemployment Rate (red)
  Unempplot <- ggplot(full_data_with_state_specific_month,
                      aes(geometry = geom, fill = unemployment_rate,
                          text = paste0(
                            "State: ", State,
                            "<br>Unemployment Rate: ",
                            round(unemployment_rate, 2), "%"))) +
    geom_sf() +
    scale_fill_distiller(type = "seq", palette = "Reds", direction = 1,
                         limits = unemp_limits) +
    theme_void() +
    labs(fill = "Unemployment (%)")

  # Side-by-side figure for one month
  fig <- plotly_build(
    subplot(
      ggplotly(Gasplot, tooltip = "text"),
      ggplotly(Unempplot, tooltip = "text"),
      nrows = 1, margin = 0.08))

  # Adjusting position of the legends by finding the legend from the traces
  # and then changing the x position.
  bar_x <- c(0.42, 1)
  cb <- 0
  for (k in seq_along(fig$x$data)) {
    if (!is.null(fig$x$data[[k]]$marker$colorbar)) {
      cb <- cb + 1
      fig$x$data[[k]]$marker$colorbar$x <- bar_x[cb]
      fig$x$data[[k]]$marker$colorbar$len <- 0.3
      fig$x$data[[k]]$marker$colorbar$lenmode <- "fraction"
    }}
  plotly_plots[[i]] <- fig
}

# This part is probably the most confusing, so I had to learn a bit about
# how Plotly works. Each month's plot has its own set of "traces",
# that together produce the two maps. We need to combine these traces so
# that Plotly knows what to display for each month.

# Empty list that will collect the traces from every month
all_traces <- list()

# Empty vector to record which month each trace came from.
trace_month <- c()

# Go through each month's plotly plot, one at a time
for (i in seq_along(plotly_plots)) {
  # Grab this month's traces and append them
  month_traces <- plotly_plots[[i]]$x$data
  all_traces <- c(all_traces, month_traces)

  # Labels where the traces came from
  trace_month <- c(trace_month, rep(i, length(month_traces)))
}

# This for loop determines which traces are initially shown (Month 1)
for (j in seq_along(all_traces)) {
  all_traces[[j]]$visible <- trace_month[j] == 1
}

# Inherit Month 1's layout, then add in all the traces
combined <- plotly_plots[[1]]
combined$x$data <- all_traces

# Create the slider and the ticker marks
tickers <- list()
for (i in seq_along(unique_months)) {
  month_name <- format(as.Date(unique_months[i]), "%B %Y")
  show_specific_month <- trace_month == i

  # Controls what occurs on each ticker
  tickers[[i]] <- list(
    method = "restyle",
    args = list("visible", show_specific_month),
    label = month_name)
}

# Attach the slider to the combined figure
combined$x$layout$sliders <- list(
  list(
    active = 0,
    currentvalue = list(prefix = "Month: "),
    x = 0.15,
    y = 0.23,
    steps = tickers))

# Centered Titles for the two maps
combined$x$layout$annotations <- list(
  list(text = "Average Regular Gas Price by State",
       x = 0.21, y = 0.73,
       xref = "paper", yref = "paper",
       showarrow = FALSE, xanchor = "center"),
  list(text = "Unemployment by State",
       x = 0.79, y = 0.7,
       xref = "paper", yref = "paper",
       showarrow = FALSE, xanchor = "center"))

# Display the final combined interactive map
combined

```
